items.heading: HERE AND THERE
items.summary: Club news column covering injuries, members' performances at summer meetings, Alan Sexton's running in America and Canada, Charlie Smart's racing in Germany, new member R. G. Plummer, and members in the Services.
items.text:
Near the end of the winter season, Eddie Short was in hospital suffering from a kick in the back, sustained while playing for the camp Rugby team, and who should be in the same R.A.F. ward but E. G. Read, our old sprint champion.

Ted was very badly knocked about in a plane crash, but is progressing after several operations, with the prospect of more to come and we wish him a full recovery from his serious injuries.

At the London v. Paris Schools meeting at the Wimbledon Park Track, Alan Law won the weight with a put of 44ft. 11¼ins., and at the same meeting our Junior team won the 1 mile medley relay open to clubs. Our team was: Frank Wright 880, T. Adams 220, J. Smith 220, J. H. Cobden 440.

Charlie Smart ran well in the Southern 6 miles track championship and in finishing 4th he recorded 30.16, which is very good running.

At the Leyton Floodlit meeting we fielded a team in the " A " section of the medley relay race and were placed 3rd to the Polytechnic H. and Achilles.

We could not field a team in the 3 miles team race, but Alan Sexton was 3rd in the 440 yds., John Bromley was 2nd to Disley in the 3,000 metres steeplechase and Frank Wright won the 1 mile Junior race in 4 mins. 29.4 secs.

Our members did well at the Charlotteville " open " meeting on Whit-Monday, and Ivan Mayers and Ian Forrester were 1st and 2nd in both the 100 and 220 yds. handicaps. We also had first two in the 880 yds., and Jim Heathfield just "pipped" Bob Wolton for 1st place. Our team of Ian Badiali, Ron Morrell, Bob Wolton and " Jock " Cameron also won the 1 mile scratch relay in the good time of 3 mins. 36.8 secs.

At the " Sward " Trophy meeting at Chiswick we had entered a team for the 2 miles team race, but only Chas. Walker put in an appearance, and he ran as an individual and was second to P. B. Driver in 9 mins. 28.8 secs.

In the Croydon v. Arnhem sports meeting we had several Club members competing, and Bill Lucas was 3rd in the 3 miles event, while Dick Savage was present as a Timekeeper.

Alan Sexton has gone to America with the Combined Universities team and won the 440 yds. in 49.9 secs., and was 3rd in the 100 yds. against the American team.

He is then going on to Canada to compete in their championships and does not expect to be back in this country until the end of August.

This means that he will miss our Club Championships and will be unable to assist us in the A.A.A. 4 x 440 yds. relay, but we wish him the best of luck in his travels.

More of our Junior members continue to go into the Services, and D. G. Hooper and T. Adams are both stationed at Hednesford in the R.A.F.

Frank Kemp is now out in the Middle East with the R.A.F., and sends best wishes to all his Club-mates. He has a brother of Basil Walden stationed with him and says he has done 10.1 for the 100 and 22.5 for the 220, so keep up the good work, Frank !

We sent a team over to the W. H. Smith & Son sports for an open 2 mile team race, and Chas. Walker was first home in 9 mins. 38 secs., with John Burr 3rd and Bill Lucas 5th, and they won the team event, beating Finchley and the Poly. H.

At the Vickers' meeting at Weybridge we again won the " Viking " Trophy, presented to the winning team in the 2 mile team race. John Bromley ran well to finish 3rd, with Jack Brown 5th, Chas. Walker 7th and Bill Lucas was our non-scoring runner.

Another success at this meeting was Ron Holtum's win in the 100 yds. open handicap event.

We are pleased to welcome R. G. Plummer, late of Oxford City A.C., to our ranks. He is a well-known long-distance runner and should strengthen our road teams once he is qualified to represent us in open competition.

Alan Sexton is now being quoted as Britain's fastest-ever runner over 440 yards. He was beaten by a yard in the Canadian National quarter-mile race by Jack Carroll, the Canadian Olympic runner, in the fast time of 47 secs.

His time was given as 47.2 secs., which is 2/5ths faster than Godfrey Brown's best-ever British performance at the White City in 1938.

The Press state that Alan only took up quarter-miling last autumn at Cambridge, apparently overlooking the fact that Alan won our 440 yds. Club championship last season.

At the Insurance A.A. championships, Percy Luxon won the High Jump with a leap of 5ft. 9ins., thus beating the best championship performance, which was put up in 1934.

Charlie Smart writes from Germany to say that he has had ten races over 5,000 metres so far this season (four of them at International meetings), and has won nine and been second to Mimoun, the French Olympic runner, in the other.

His last two races were in the B.A.O.R. Championship, which he won in 14.55 (a new record), and at an International meeting near Saarbrucken also in 14.55, which is a new Saarland record.

These times for 5,000 metres are equivalent to 14.23 for 3 miles, and Charlie says that the standard of German distance running cannot compare with present U.K. times.

We offer our sincere congratulations to Eric Bishop on his recent marriage. Eric does a very good job of work in getting the prizes and medals for the various Club races.

Our Pole Vaulter, Van Sukavachana, competed in an invitation event at the Heathfield meeting, and although he cleared the same height as the winner, he was placed 3rd on the number of failures.

Congratulations to Hugh McGreechan on winning the Surrey W.C. 14 miles Keston race on March 21st, and also winning the Police Long Distance Championship—Barking to Southend—for the third time.

Harry Shields won the London Transport 10 miles Championship, with Bill Wesson 2nd, on April 7th.

Gerry Warr was 2nd in the University one mile at Motspur Park on May 7th.

Charlie Speechley—like Johnny Walker—still going strong, won the handicap in the Veterans' match at Parliament Hill on May 20th.

Percy Wright was 2nd and Gerry Warr 3rd in the Hampshire County 2 miles Championship.

Ted Smith took second place in the Business Houses 2 miles Track Walk on July 15th in 15 mins. 24 secs.

George Oliver won the Civil Service 2 miles Track Championship on July 18th.

Gerry Warr has now gone into the R.A.F. for his National Service.

At the National Schools Championships at Uxbridge, John Powell-Jones was competing for Surrey in the Senior Weight, and he won with a putt of 45ft. 1½ins.

P. L. Porter won the Essex Hammer Throw and is improving each time out.

We have heard that Don Maclean and Geoff Goode are now both out in Korea, while Ian Forrester is also serving in the Far East, and we hope that these lads will still retain their interest in running once their enforced absence is at an end.

At the Civil Service championships, Jack Brown won the 1 mile, beating Len Eyre, while Bob Taylor won the 880 yds. in 1 min. 56.9 secs.

At the newly-opened Croydon Track was held an Inter-County match and we had four winners at this meeting, as follows : Bob Taylor (Middx.), 880 ; Jack Brown (Kent), 1 mile ; T. J. Gaworski (Surrey), Weight ; K. C. Key (Middx.), Long Jump.

John Bromley won the Army steeplechase title in a new record time, and was 3rd in the Inter-Services event, with Eddie Short (R.A.F.) in second place.

Peter Casselton, our Junior 440 yds. champion, is now in Germany with the B.A.O.R., and ran in the championships out there, but found that Army life is not good training for running.

The Wandsworth Council promoted a 14 miles road run in connection with their Coronation celebrations, and Geoff Pearson finished 3rd, with Len Rolls 8th and Bert Smith 15th.

E. M. Bare, our high jumper, competed for an A.A.A. team at Eastbourne in a match against a combined Sussex and Kent side, and was second in the high jump with a leap of 6ft.

R. J. Harris, our former Discus champion, is now in Singapore with the R.A.F., and at a recent Inter-Services meeting he did 40ft. 9ins. with the Shot, and over 125ft. in the Discus, and he should be an asset to the growing strength of our field event section on his return to civvy street.
